summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes, morbid obesity, atrial fibrillation, and chronic foot ulcers was admitted with chills and found to have gas gangrene of the right first toe. He underwent amputation and a subsequent debridement with wound vac placement. His postoperative course was complicated by sepsis, hypotension, and acute kidney injury, requiring ICU monitoring. He was treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to ertapenem via PICC line for six weeks. His heart failure was managed with diuresis, and his warfarin was adjusted after an elevated INR. He was stabilized and discharged to an extended care facility for ongoing IV antibiotic therapy and wound care.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Diabetes with peripheral circulatory disorders, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Ulcer of other part of foot
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
